subject: SIG: breach notification timing — kickoff & evidence checklist
messages:
From: Alex Chen <sec_ops@greenfintech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Yu <rachel.yu@greenfintech.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questions — breach notification timing & evidence

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the SIG questionnaire for a procurement review and one of the core items is the incident response / breach notification section. A few specific asks we need to clarify so we can map answers back to our internal risk categories: 

- The SIG asks for your standard timeframe to notify customers of a confirmed data breach. Do you commit to a 72-hour notification window after confirmation? If there are exceptions, what are they (e.g., law enforcement, forensic requirements)?
- What artifacts can Redwood provide as evidence for an incident (redacted IR timelines, SOC 2 evidence, audit logs, FFIEC-style timelines)? Is there a standard evidence bundle you share?
- Who is your primary POC for security notifications (phone + email) and what is your escalation chain for incidents that meet "Severity 1 / Data exfiltration" thresholds?
- Any legal / contractual constraints we should be aware of if we request forensic images or raw logs?

We'd like to do a short kickoff call to align expectations and request the evidence bundle if possible. Can you share a read-only link or a secure transfer method? Our timeline is tight — procurement needs SIG answers by 2027-05-20.

Appreciate it —
Alex Chen
Sr. Security Operations
GreenFintech
sec_ops@greenfintech.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <sec_ops@greenfintech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG questions — breach notification timing & evidence

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers here and then a proposal for next steps / attachments.

1) Notification window: we aim to notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirmed data breach where confirmation means we have validated unauthorized access to customer data and completed an initial triage. Exceptions: notifications may be delayed for short periods to preserve forensic integrity or at the request of law enforcement; in those cases we commit to communicating about the delay and expected timeframe. Final contractual language is subject to legal review (see Karthik cc'd).

2) Evidence we can provide:
- Redacted IR timeline (we redact PII and sensitive internal artifacts)
- SOC 2 Type II attestation and summary report (we attach the SOC 2 cover pages / control matrix references in the evidence bundle)
- Audit logs (redacted/time-windowed extracts) and API access logs with hashes; we do not transfer raw forensic disk images over email but can provide hashes and a secure transfer process if required for legal/regulatory review.

3) Primary POC / escalation:
- Primary incident contact: Marcus Lin, Product Security Lead — marcus_lin@redwood.com, +1 (650) 555-0123
- Escalation (S1 / Data exfiltration): Neha Kapoor (VP, Security) -> Karthik Iyer (Legal) -> Grace O'Connor (Customer Success for account coordination).

4) Legal constraints: requests for full forensic artifacts require an approved data handling agreement and may require an NDA and a documented chain-of-custody. We'll share a template access agreement for that.

Next steps: I attached a short evidence checklist and a redacted IR playbook extract. I'll provision a read-only folder with the evidence bundle; link below. Proposed internal owners: Karthik will review any contract/exception language, Grace will coordinate delivery to your CS/Procurement team. Can you confirm GreenFintech's preferred evidence delivery mechanism (Drive share versus SFTP)?

Proposed timeline: compile and share redacted bundle by 2027-05-16 to meet your 05-20 deadline. If that works for you we'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff tomorrow (Wed 05-12) 10am PT.

Attachments: redwood_sig_response_v1.pdf; ir_playbook_redacted.pdf; evidence_collection_instructions.txt
Link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/s/greenfintech-evidence-share

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Product Security Lead
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0123

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700

Marcus —

Thanks, that helps a lot. Quick follow-ups after reviewing the checklist: 

- SLA exceptions: for procurement we need a short blurb that explains the process and confirmation cadence if the 72-hour window is delayed for forensics. Can Karthik provide an example clause or language?
- Executive notification: do you have a commitment to notify an executive sponsor at the customer (we'll provide sponsor contact) for incidents that meet our "Full Account Compromise" definition?
- Evidence handoff: Drive link is fine but we prefer SFTP for anything containing logs; can you confirm you'll accept SFTP pull with a one-time token?

Also CC'ing Rachel (legal) — she's reviewing whether the forensic image request would trigger additional contract terms.

Best,
Alex

Subject: Re: SIG questions — breach notification timing & evidence

Alex / Rachel —

Quick responses inline and a proposed notification / escalation blurb you can include in the SIG answers doc.

- SLA exceptions language (draft): "Redwood will notify affected customers of confirmed data breaches within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation. Notification may be delayed to preserve forensic integrity or at the request of law enforcement; Redwood will provide contemporaneous status updates, including an estimated notification date, and engage the customer's designated point of contact within the initial 72-hour window where feasible." Karthik, please treat as draft legal language.

- Executive notification: yes — we can add an executive escalation path. When a customer indicates an executive sponsor in procurement, we will add that contact to the incident distribution list for any incident classified as Full Account Compromise or higher.

- Evidence handoff / SFTP: we support SFTP pull with one-time tokens for log extracts and redacted archives. For anything requiring forensic chain-of-custody (disk images, raw memory), we'll require an access agreement and escorted transfer.

Action items: 
- (Marcus) Provision read-only evidence folder and share SFTP endpoint details by 2027-05-14.
- (Karthik) Draft final SIG clause for the procurement team by 2027-05-14.
- (Grace) Coordinate delivery schedule and confirm GreenFintech's preferred SFTP contact by 2027-05-12 end of day.

I'll also attach the short blurb for the SIG questionnaire (redwood_sig_response_v1.pdf) for you to paste into your response. If you want a short 15-minute alignment before we hand over artifacts, I'm available tomorrow 10:00–11:00 PT.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
